# The Common Writ The sector's law, upheld by the Bench: the judges of Caelestinus Central. It binds everyone within the anchors and beyond them, and not knowing it is no defence.
## Penalties - [bold]Citation[/bold]: a fine. - [bold]Impound[/bold]: a fine, and the vessel is held at Central until the Bench releases it. - [bold]Banishment[/bold]: a fine, and the offender is barred from Caelestinus Central. - [bold]Outlawry[/bold]: no fine. The offender is Wanted, with a bounty on the board, and anyone may bring them before the Bench.
## Article I: Crimes against Reality - [bold]Breach of the Anchors[/bold] (Outlawry): Raising a hand, weapon or tool against an anchor, its shield or its wardens, or cutting the power to a sanctioned relay. - [bold]Trespass beyond the Anchors[/bold] (Citation, 10,000; a judge may set 5,000 to 20,000): Entering Dissonance or Feedback space without a Coda Writ. - [bold]Trespass in the Coda[/bold] (Impound, 60,000; a judge may set 50,000 to 100,000): Entering the Coda without a Bench-sanctioned expedition. - [bold]Unsanctioned Landing[/bold] (Impound, 50,000; a judge may set 30,000 to 80,000): Entering orbit around, or landing on, a world the Bench has not sanctioned. - [bold]Quarantine Breach[/bold] (Banishment, 100,000; a judge may set 75,000 to 150,000): Landing on a quarantine world, or carrying anything off one. - [bold]Possession of Unlawful Material[/bold] (Citation, 15,000; a judge may set 10,000 to 25,000): Holding unlawful material for personal use: a shard, a charm, a token. - [bold]Trafficking in Unlawful Material[/bold] (Impound, 75,000; a judge may set 50,000 to 120,000): Mining, refining, selling, carrying in bulk or fitting unlawful material to a vessel. - [bold]Harbouring an Artifact[/bold] (Outlawry): Keeping, powering or wiring into a vessel any unregistered object recovered beyond the anchors. - [bold]Sedition against the Anchors[/bold] (Outlawry): Preaching the unmooring of the sector, or belonging to any congregation that does.
[bold]Unlawful material[/bold] is exotic matter, raw or refined, and anything built from it; any object recovered beyond the anchors that bears no registry mark, or that is warm, hums or gives power without a source; and remains recovered beyond the anchors that were not returned through the Bench. Surrendering it to the Bench is never a crime.
## Schedule of Unlawful Material What the Bench seizes under Article I. Each is marked as unlawful when examined. - [bold]Exotic matter[/bold]: exotic matter in any form; the Drift stabiliser and its flatpack; the anchor charm; the relay anchor and its flatpack, unless built under a Bench licence. - [bold]Black stones[/bold]: a monolith scion, a monolith shard, a monolith splinter, and any monolith tap or other console wired to one. - [bold]Remains[/bold]: the bodies and severed parts of the Remade, and anything taken off a quarantine world.
## Article II: Crimes against persons and vessels - [bold]Murder[/bold] (Banishment, 100,000; a judge may set 75,000 to 150,000): Unlawfully killing a person. - [bold]Assault[/bold] (Citation, 10,000; a judge may set 5,000 to 25,000): Unlawfully harming a person. - [bold]Piracy[/bold] (Impound, 75,000; a judge may set 50,000 to 120,000): Harpooning, pinning, boarding or stripping a vessel without its crew's consent. - [bold]Hull Theft[/bold] (Impound, 75,000; a judge may set 50,000 to 120,000): Flying, selling or breaking a vessel without its deed, or dealing in its parts.
## Article III: Crimes against the Bench - [bold]Failing to Heave To[/bold] (Impound, 50,000; a judge may set 30,000 to 80,000): Ignoring or fleeing a judge's hail. - [bold]Contempt of the Bench[/bold] (Outlawry): Attacking or impersonating a judge, or escaping their custody. - [bold]False Distress[/bold] (Citation, 20,000; a judge may set 10,000 to 30,000): Sending a distress call where there is none. - [bold]Unsanctioned Warheads[/bold] (Outlawry): Arming a warhead without the authority of a faction's command in time of declared war.
## Article IV: Ordinances of Caelestinus Central - [bold]Brandishing[/bold] (Citation, 5,000; a judge may set 2,000 to 10,000): Carrying a weapon drawn, unholstered or unbagged aboard Central. - [bold]Discharge[/bold] (Banishment, 100,000; a judge may set 75,000 to 150,000): Firing a weapon aboard Central. - [bold]Breach of Neutral Ground[/bold] (Banishment, 100,000; a judge may set 75,000 to 150,000): Waging faction war aboard Central, or within its sanctuary. - [bold]Docking Order[/bold] (Citation, 10,000; a judge may set 5,000 to 20,000): Docking against the dockmaster's word, or keeping ship weapons hot within the sanctuary. - [bold]Undeclared Material[/bold] (Citation, 25,000; a judge may set 15,000 to 40,000): Failing to declare unlawful material on docking. Charged together with Article I. - [bold]Concealment[/bold] (Citation, 5,000; a judge may set 2,000 to 10,000): Refusing to show identification to a judge.
## General clauses - [bold]Drift is no defence.[/bold] A judge may weigh it in setting the penalty, never in deciding guilt. - [bold]Declared war.[/bold] While war is declared, Murder, Assault and Piracy do not apply between combatants of the warring factions. Never for neutrals or Vagrants, and never aboard Central. - [bold]Salvage right.[/bold] A vessel is derelict only when no holder of its deed is aboard or nearby and it has gone unclaimed for twenty minutes. - [bold]Custom charges.[/bold] The Bench may post ordinances for the round, or bring a charge not written here. - [bold]Pardon.[/bold] Only the Bench may pardon a ticket. A pardon returns everything that was taken.
## Tickets Judges ticket from the Bench app on their PDA, or a Bench terminal. The offender must be standing close by. The fine comes out of their account straight away and the judge hands them the stamped ticket. - Whatever they can't pay is Bench debt. Half of everything they earn goes to it until it is cleared. - Debt still owed after 30 minutes, or over 50,000, marks them Wanted until it is paid. - An Outlawry ticket marks them Wanted at once and puts a bounty on them. - The Bench's limits: a law counts once per ticket, one ticket fines at most 200,000, and nobody is fined more than 400,000 in a round. Past that, the ticket still stands but the fine stops.
